<!-- CORE-COMPONENTS-CN-START -->
**Core shared class helper:** consume the existing helper through the shared UI
boundary:

```tsx
import { cn } from "@asym/ui/lib/utils";
```

Do not create a competing local `cn` implementation or add `clsx`/`tailwind-merge`
for these recipes. The generic npm dependency examples below are retained
upstream material and are **non-operative in Core**. Current workspace manifests
and `packages/ui/lib/utils.ts` own the implementation and dependency choices.
<!-- CORE-COMPONENTS-CN-END -->

replacements.upstream: 7. **Intelligent Class Merging** - Use `cn()` utility with tailwind-merge
7. **Intelligent Class Merging** - Use `cn()` utility with tailwind-merge
Use Tailwind CSS with intelligent class merging (`tailwind-merge`), conditional classes (`clsx`), and variant APIs (CVA).
replacements.core: Use Tailwind CSS with Core’s shared `cn` helper for class merging and conditional classes, and existing variant APIs (CVA).

replacements.upstream: **Why:** Without `tailwind-merge`, conflicting classes both apply. The `cn` utility resolves conflicts intelligently.
replacements.core: **Why:** Core’s shared `cn` helper resolves class conflicts consistently with the installed UI implementation.

replacements.upstream: // Without tailwind-merge, conflicting classes both apply
replacements.core: // Without class merging, conflicting classes both apply

import { cn } from "@asym/ui/lib/utils";

cn("bg-red-500", "bg-blue-500"); // "bg-blue-500"
cn("px-4 py-2", "px-8"); // "py-2 px-8"
cn("text-sm", "text-lg"); // "text-lg"
